body:
Parent: #6022 (placement policy). Related: #6062 (ID-graph publication format), #6267 (note_submission pilot), #3125 (provenance registry), #5669 (Atlas staging and sensitivity tiers).

Implement the placement policy from #6022 in the existing note_submission pipeline. This issue does not redefine the submission envelope or ID relation vocabulary, and it does not replace the #6267 pilot or #6062 publication-format design.

## Scope
- Classify submissions into the canonical home chosen by the placement policy: workspace/memory (not published), repo document, registry-selected Zettelkasten corpus, or ID-native publication when the #6022/#6062 eligibility and format are satisfied.
- Keep each submission in the Turso submission DB with content hash and provenance spans; preserve source system, machine, date, author/owner and sensitivity decision.
- Enforce staged review and human promotion. Uncertain classification or sensitivity remains staged; nothing auto-commits or auto-promotes.
- Record canonical identity and source revision/hash on any approved projection; maintain an auditable mapping of source to destination.
- Use Atlas physical tiers `public`, `internal`, and `secret` only after applying the separate source/caller sensitivity ceiling. Default to `internal`; public/secret changes are explicit.

## Acceptance
- Table-driven tests cover every note class in #6022's decision table and their selected destination, Atlas treatment, and ID-native eligibility.
- Uncertain/unsupported destinations stay staged and are not published.
- Approval is rechecked immediately before publication; rejected/held attempts leave an audit record and do not push.
- Repo and Zettelkasten projections preserve provenance and cannot silently become a second canonical owner.
- ID-native publication calls the format from #6062 and existing writer/capability authority; no parallel relation or permission schema is introduced.
- A small end-to-end test proves stage → human approval → selected destination and verifies content hash/provenance against the submission record.

## Dependencies
Blocked by #6022 design review/merge and #6062 publication-format decision. Reuse the #6267 submission DB pilot.

## Acceptance criteria

- Submissions are classified into exactly the #6022 canonical homes (workspace/memory unpublished, repo document, registry-selected Zettelkasten corpus, ID-native publication when #6022/#6062 eligibility + format are met).
- Every submission stays in the Turso submission DB with content hash, provenance spans, source system/machine/date, author/owner, and its sensitivity decision.
- Uncertain classification or sensitivity remains staged: nothing auto-commits or auto-promotes, and promotion is a recorded human action.
- Any approved projection records its canonical identity and source revision/hash, and the audit trail can reconstruct who promoted what, when, and why.
